scenes.line1: How do you trust API data?
scenes.say: How do you make sure your API data is safe? Can TypeScript really catch bad inputs when your code runs?

scenes.label: Runtime
scenes.say: TypeScript types only exist while you code. When your app runs, those types are gone.

scenes.code:
import { z } from 'zod'
const UserSchema = z.object({
  id: z.number(),
  name: z.string()
})
type User = z.infer<typeof UserSchema>
UserSchema.parse({ id: 1, name: 'Alice' })
scenes.say: With zod, you define a schema for your data. It checks values at runtime and gives you a matching TypeScript type.
TypeScript checks types while you code. Zod checks real data when your app runs. Both matter for API safety.

scenes.question: Is TypeScript enough for API validation?
scenes.right: No, TypeScript only checks types at compile-time. Use zod for runtime validation.
scenes.say: Is TypeScript enough to keep your API data safe? No, you need runtime checks with zod or similar libraries.
